The two small plan documents were generated by the pinned Ptah CLI commit
`f6e562c5b0986cd29a53a5cc01938827336b780a` against isolated PostgreSQL 17
and MySQL 8.4 databases. The executor was built with this repository's
`Dockerfile.executor`. These are standalone native CLI fixture measurements;
they do not supply Kubernetes or production acceptance.

The SQL source contains 32 `<` bytes in defaults. PostgreSQL uses one TEXT
column. MySQL distributes the total over 100 VARCHAR(16000) columns in a fixed
table set: the pinned source parser cannot accept the expression required by
a MySQL TEXT default. All native plans are non-destructive CREATE TABLE
statements, with no padding or edited plan bytes in the CLI probes.

Adding one `<` byte increases the saved native JSON by six bytes; adding one
`x` increases it by one. The PostgreSQL envelope is 592 bytes and the MySQL
envelope is 27,517 bytes. Independently generated full CLI plans measured
8,388,608 and 8,388,609 bytes on both engines. Native OCI-layout publication
and pull preserved those sizes after canonical HCL conversion. Publication
ran with a 256 MiB memory limit; native Plan and Apply ran with 512 MiB.
Both maximum plans applied through the native CLI. PostgreSQL executed its
default in an inserted row; MySQL retained all 100 exact defaults.

The predicate unit tests expand only these fixtures' default literals while
preserving the other native bytes. The cluster scenario calibrates with real
operator-produced plans, publishes generated SQL, and requires actual native
Plan, storage, approval, projection and Apply evidence. Its oversized refusal
must report a saved file of exactly 8,388,609 bytes and no executable storage,
unauthorized SQL or Apply.
